newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle rebound, finish higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle rebound, finish higher.

text.p: CME feeder cattle futures rallied to higher closes as short covering triggered fund buy stops. Live cattle also posted closing gains, bolstered by a strong tone in cash cattle markets, traders said.
Feeder cattle closed 0.650 to 0.050 cent per lb higher with May up most at 71.650 cents. Live cattle finished up 0.475 to 0.100 with April up most and June up 0.375 at 65.250 cents.

Short covering sparked by a lack of selling interest despite higher corn futures and a lower CME index pushed feeder cattle futures up into fund buy stops. Strong cash ideas kept futures supported, traders said.
USDA reported that feeder cattle sold steady to $1.00 per cwt higher Monday at the key Oklahoma City auction.

Interest for feeders is expected to continue. Stronger fed cattle indications should keep interest for replacement cattle up. Also, grazing conditions have improved and recent death losses in the northern Plains was supportive to back months in the feeder pit, traders said.

"If we did get some damage from this freeze in the wheat area, it may open up demand for some calves to put on some of this wheat and graze it out," said Tom Tippens, CEO of Oklahoma-based Professional Cattle Consultants also noted.
The latest CME feeder cattle index fell $0.22 to $70.97 per cwt and another $0.50 loss was seen on the next quote.
LIT division of First Options, E.D.&F. Man and Lind-Waldock actively bought on the rally, pit sources said.
Live cattle futures followed feeders higher as a strong undertone to cash markets provided support and lifted June through technical resistance, traders said.

Wholesale beef values hit two-week highs at midday and packers were expected to pay at least another $1 per cwt higher for cash cattle soon. Gains could be even greater if beef sales remain strong after last week's brisk pace, they said.
USDA last week reported beef sales on 434 loads of fabricated cuts Tuesday, 452 loads Wednesday, 313 loads Thursday and 273 loads Friday.
"I still think there is a chance we'll trade $68 and possibly $69 cattle this week," said David Holloway, market analyst for Koch Beef Company.
Cargill Investor Services, LIT division of First Options, R.J. O'Brien and locals bought late, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, there was commercial hedging in August, buying 64 and 66 puts. Commission house sold June 66 to 68 calls and 61 and 62 puts, pit sources added.
